{{Short description|Type of improper integral with general solution}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Frullani integrals''' (also called '''Cauchy–Frullani integrals'''<ref>{{cite journal|author=[[Alexander Ostrowski]]|title=On some generalizations of the Cauchy–Frullani integral|journal=[[PNAS]]|volume=35|year=1949|page=612-616|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1063092/pdf/pnas01547-0068.pdf}}</ref>) are a specific type of [[improper integral]] named after the Italian mathematician [[Giuliano Frullani]] (and the french mathematician [[Augustin Cauchy]]). The integrals are of the form
:<math>\int _{0}^{\infty}{\frac {f(ax)-f(bx)}{x}}\,{\rm {d}}x</math>
where <math>f</math> is a [[Function (mathematics)|function]] defined for all non-negative [[real number]]s that has a [[Limit of a function#Limits at infinity|limit]] at <math>\infty</math>, which we denote by <math>f(\infty)</math>.

The formula below appears without proof in a letter from Frullani dated 1821 and was proved by Cauchy in 1823.<ref> {{cite journal |last=Cauchy |first=Augustin-Louis |author-link=Augustin-Louis Cauchy |year=1823 |title=Mémoire sur l'intégration des équations linéaires aux différentielles partielles et à coefficients constants |journal=Journal de l'École polytechnique |at=p. 576 |url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k433675h/f578.item}} (''Œuvres complètes'', [https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k90193x/f345.item series 2, volume 1, pp. 275–357: p. 339])</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Arias-de-Reyna |first=Juan |year=1990 |title=On the Theorem of Frullani |journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |volume=109 |issue=1 |pages=165–175 |url=https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/d180/9763d40f6f173752cfe57d1ba3a61e30124a.pdf}}</ref>

The following formula for their general solution holds if <math>f</math> is continuous on <math>(0,\infty)</math>, has finite limit at <math>\infty</math>, and <math>a,b > 0</math>:

:<math>\int _{0}^{\infty }{\frac {f(ax)-f(bx)}{x}}\,{\rm {d}}x=\Big(f(\infty)-f(0)\Big)\ln {\frac {a}{b}}.</math>
If <math>f (\infty)</math> does not exist, but <math>\int_c^\infty \frac{f(x)}{x} dx</math> exists for some <math>c > 0</math>, then <math display="block">\int _{0}^{\infty }{\frac {f(ax)-f(bx)}{x}}\,{\rm {d}}x= -f(0)\ln {\frac {a}{b}}.</math>

== Proof for continuously differentiable functions==

A simple proof of the formula (under stronger assumptions than those stated above, namely <math>f \in \mathcal{C}^1(0,\infty)</math>) can be arrived at by using the [[Fundamental theorem of calculus]] to express the [[integrand]] as an integral of <math>f'(xt) = \frac{\partial }{\partial t} \left(\frac{f(xt)}{x}\right)</math>:

:<math>\begin{align}
  \frac{f(ax)-f(bx)}{x} &= \left[\frac{f(xt)}{x}\right]_{t=b}^{t=a} \, \\
   & = \int_b^a f'(xt) \, dt \\
 \end{align}</math>

and then use [[Fubini's theorem#Tonelli's theorem|Tonelli’s theorem]] to interchange the two integrals:

:<math>\begin{align}
  \int_0^\infty \frac{f(ax)-f(bx)}{x} \,dx 
   & = \int_0^\infty \int_b^a f'(xt) \, dt \, dx \\
   & = \int_b^a \int_0^\infty f'(xt) \, dx \, dt \\
   & = \int_b^a \left[\frac{f(xt)}{t}\right]_{x=0}^{x \to \infty}\, dt \\
   & = \int_b^a \frac{f(\infty)-f(0)}{t}\, dt \\
   & = \Big(f(\infty)-f(0)\Big)\Big(\ln(a)-\ln(b)\Big) \\
   & = \Big(f(\infty)-f(0)\Big)\ln\Big(\frac{a}{b}\Big) \\
 \end{align}</math>
Note that the integral in the second line above has been taken over the [[Interval (mathematics)|interval]] <math>[b,a]</math>, not <math>[a,b]</math>.

== Ramanujan's generalization ==
Ramanujan, using his [[Ramanujan's master theorem|master theorem]], gave the following generalization.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Berndt |first1=Bruce |last2=Dixit |first2=Atul |date=2021-05-06 |title=Ramanujan's Beautiful Integrals |url=https://hrj.episciences.org/7429 |journal=Hardy-Ramanujan Journal |language=en |volume=43|department=Special Commemorative volume in honour of Srinivasa Ramanujan – 2020 |doi=10.46298/hrj.2021.7429 |arxiv=2103.14002 |issn=2804-7370}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berndt |first=Bruce C. |date=October 1983 |title=The Quarterly Reports of S. Ramanujan |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00029890.1983.11971272 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |language=en |volume=90 |issue=8 |pages=505–516 |doi=10.1080/00029890.1983.11971272 |issn=0002-9890|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Let <math>f, g</math> be functions continuous on <math>[0, \infty]</math>.<math display="block">
f(x)-f(\infty)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{u(k)(-x)^k}{k!} \quad \text { and } \quad g(x)-g(\infty)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{v(k)(-x)^k}{k!}
</math>Let <math display="inline">u(x)</math> and <math display="inline">v(x)</math> be given as above, and assume that <math display="inline">f</math> and <math display="inline">g</math> are continuous functions on <math display="inline">[0, \infty)</math>. Also assume that <math display="inline">f(0)=g(0)</math> and <math display="inline">f(\infty)=g(\infty)</math>. Then, if <math display="inline">a, b>0</math>,

<math display="block">
\lim _{n \rightarrow 0} \int_0^{\infty} x^{n-1}\{f(a x)-g(b x)\} d x=\{f(0)-f(\infty)\}\left\{\log \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)+\frac{d}{d s}\left(\log \left(\frac{v(s)}{u(s)}\right)\right)_{s=0}\right\}
</math>

== Applications ==
The formula can be used to derive an integral representation for the [[natural logarithm]] <math>\ln(x)</math> by letting <math>f(x) = e^{-x}</math> and <math>a=1</math>:

:<math>{\int _{0}^{\infty}{\frac {e^{-x}-e^{-bx}}{x}}\,{\rm {d}}x=\Big(\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{e^n}-e^0\Big)\ln \Big({\frac {1}{b}}}\Big) = \ln(b)</math>

The formula can also be generalized in several different ways.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bravo |first1=Sergio |last2=Gonzalez |first2=Ivan |last3=Kohl |first3=Karen |last4=Moll |first4=Victor Hugo |author-link4=Victor Hugo Moll |title=Integrals of Frullani type and the method of brackets |journal=Open Mathematics |date=21 January 2017 |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=1–12 |doi=10.1515/math-2017-0001 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
